state.goal: Release only the missing mounted Identity/Interfaces/Cloudflare browser request and revocation boundary contract, preserving existing auth/evaluation/recovery. No global backend, epoch, deployment activation or whole-security acceptance.
verified_source: Login GET rate-limits then mints a ten-minute opaque single-use token stored hashed. Descriptor JSON gives the raw token; POST JSON/form consumes presented token before password checking. It currently has no browser cookie binding. An attacker can obtain a token in their own browser; secrecy of each descriptor alone does not bind the victim browser.

Ordinary Interfaces auth bodies use existing streaming 1048576-byte JSON/form caps. Session-cookie mutations use the session-bound CSRF header or field. Cookies are host-scoped HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure by default; explicit local HTTP opts out. No Origin enforcement exists in these helpers.

Mounted production POST /mcp/grants bypasses Interfaces. It resolves cookie session/current active membership before unbounded req.json(), then issues a grant; it checks no content type, CSRF or Origin. Valid JSON text can be supplied as a simple-request content type. SameSite and same-origin response reading constrain attacks; no generic bearer exfiltration is established.

Production already accepts an explicit canonical HTTP(S) CAN_AUTH_ORIGIN and derives auth origin/secure cookie policy from it. Grant mount currently forwards only identityStore, not that trusted auth configuration. Public request URL/Host is not the chosen trusted-origin source.

OAuth authorize GET is descriptor-only; POST is capped JSON, current session/team and session CSRF, then exact client/redirect/43-character S256 validation and issue. Public registration and token exchange are separate: capped JSON registration; form/JSON token exchange plus matching single-use code/client/redirect/PKCE verifier. No ambient cookie authorizes exchange.

MCP transport authenticates an explicit grant Bearer and audience before SDK body parsing; cookie/presession do not authenticate it. Mutation dispatch rereads credential after arguments/permission and immediately before invoker entry; read/discovery lack this second mutation check.

Credential reread returns no atomic fence or revision token. HTTP has the same pre-invoker liveness boundary. Identity revocation does not change the separate team State revision. The source cannot guarantee cancellation if revocation completes after invoker entry but before eventual effects/commit.

state.problem: Choose an explicit idempotent chunk contract for a bounded, authenticated, append-only binary upload API. This is an abstract programming design question, without code, identifiers, deployment locations, credentials or application data.
required_outcomes: A lost reply after committed partial or complete upload can be retried without appending duplicate bytes.
Identical bytes intentionally sent at the next offset append normally.
Wrong offset, gaps, partially overlapping ranges and changed bytes under an earlier range refuse without effects.
Retry correctness survives reopening storage and serialized competing clients.
A retry of a complete transfer can recover completion evidence before finalization. Terminal rejected, expired or finalized uploads remain closed.
No unbounded per-request metadata growth, implicit current-offset inference or weakening actual byte count/digest checks.
available_mechanisms: The selected durable binding runs synchronous blob and upload metadata mutations within one real SQLite transaction. Separate external filesystem and metadata ports cannot share that transaction.
Uploads are bounded by an existing byte ceiling. The current byte port can read a copied bounded staging buffer and its size.
The API can require a canonical nonnegative safe integer byte offset. Content length comes from the actual chunk bytes.

candidates.range_identity: Require offset. New bytes append only when offset equals the committed length. A fully covered prior range succeeds only when its exact stored bytes match the supplied bytes; its deterministic acknowledgment is the range end. Gap, partial overlap or mismatch refuses. Intent plus offset/length/exact bytes defines retry identity; no nonce history. Empty chunk is a zero-effect request. Current completion status is distinct from range acknowledgment. Transaction serializes validation and writes.
candidates.nonce_ledger: Require stable chunk nonce and offset. Persist every nonce with offset, length, digest and original acknowledgment in the same transaction as bytes/count. Matching nonce replay returns stored acknowledgment; conflicting reuse refuses. New identical bytes at the next offset use a new nonce. Impose an explicit maximum ledger size or minimum chunk size so zero-byte/tiny chunks cannot cause unbounded metadata.
candidates.defer: Do not release retry-safe upload until an independently required producer or storage capability is identified. Preserve existing duplicate-unsafe append only with an explicit limitation; does not satisfy the requested full retry outcome now.

state.problem: Choose the necessary host-contract direction for crash-safe physical file garbage collection while preserving committed reference safety. This is an abstract storage design question; no source code, deployment identifiers, user data or credentials are included.
verified_topology: Reference records use owner-scoped D1 stores. Each store has a monotonic revision and atomically commits a revision assertion together with its writes in one database batch. It has no interactive or cross-database transaction.

Finalized file metadata and bytes use a separate SQLite database. Its synchronous transaction rolls back together; it rejects async callbacks. Current deletion marks terminal metadata and deletes bytes together. Public finalization never revives a terminal file identity.
A complete bounded reference census captures an original State revision. Async revalidation detects drift at its read but does not hold a lock through deletion.

Ordinary State commit and migration publication both change live record references. Existing owner routing is trusted host configuration. No common durable deletion coordinator or all-writer retirement guard is implemented.
Current file identities and receiving owner scope are immutable. Multiple references, nested values, collections and archived rows count until disposal. A single attachment marker is not a census.
requirements: A newly committed reference must not win after a deletion decision that authorizes irreversible byte removal. A writer racing the decision either wins before a fresh complete census or refuses atomically without partial effects.

Crash after retirement decision but before or during physical deletion must recover from persisted facts. Reopening must not revive the identity. Stale writers and stale deletion attempts must refuse against actual original scope and immutable identity.
Every live-reference writer, including migration publication, must participate. No process-local mutex, observation followed by sweep, lease expiry alone, or post-deletion revalidation qualifies.
Preserve required D1 and Files SQLite engines, existing authorization and retention policy; no implicit backend switch, native preparation, deployment or publication.

deletion_host_contract.source_base: ecc46d57b477f8f6535864f219063ea2fa176637; Capability fae7a4a103434742f102783e9887c9c75d9637d0 read as prerequisite evidence only, not imported
contract: State publishes permanent retirement under the SAME atomic fence as the original complete committed reference census revision and installed canonical declaration correspondence. Census includes every permitted nested, collection, nullable, optional and archived occurrence. Policy eligibility remains the existing retention contract; an attachment marker cannot replace it.

Before retirement, a competing reference writer either commits and defeats the original revision (requiring a new complete census), or loses to retirement and refuses atomically. After retirement, every newly introduced live reference to the retired identity refuses at the actual State storage write boundary. This is a permanent admission barrier, not a lease, detached observation or revalidate-then-sweep adapter.

Bind durable retirement to exact app/team/State owner, trusted physical Files store/receiver mapping and immutable File identity/finalization correspondence. Original decision identity, evidence and terminal disposition persist on retries. A stale, altered, copied or wrong-store DTO cannot mint retirement authority; reopening must resolve the genuine persisted issuer.

Files consumes only that genuine persisted decision, rechecks exact immutable physical correspondence, and saves terminal metadata plus removes bytes inside the existing Files transaction. A crash after State retirement leaves the admission barrier closed and resumes idempotent physical cleanup. Completed cleanup never reopens/reissues the original identity; stale or mismatched cleanup refuses before effects.

All ordinary commits, migration publication (including rows staged before retirement), and installed-schema activation that can reinterpret values as File slots participate. Legacy/raw callers without the checked profile refuse instead of bypassing admission. Staging alone is not live admission; activation must establish the same installed-declaration/census relationship or refuse.

All reference writers for a physical File must resolve to the same authoritative State store and genuine durable issuer; another owner pin, cloned database or process handle cannot substitute for it. A profile spanning additional State stores remains unsupported without durable admission atomic with every affected commit. Every physical deleter participates in that authority. Current low-level Files retention APIs prove only Files-local behavior; do not expose them as qualified cross-store cleanup. No detached-byte revocation or return-time disclosure guarantee is added.

No full row data or bearer in token; UI carries one opaque token. Commit recomputes the exact table under current checked source and compares authenticated digest before any row invocation. Expired reviews need renewed review while caller operation IDs remain unchanged for canonical receipt replay; do not restore an expired review as authority.

Two signed variants have equal claims, denial, row-digest, key ownership, bounded token and per-row admission semantics: a separate CSV binding factory/HttpDeps port configured by host, or a dedicated csvReview sub-port returned by the existing host-key SourceFormBindings provider. The sub-port adds only purpose-specific CSV seal/verify and preserves specialized form seal/restore unchanged; absent sub-port refuses CSV rather than unsigned fallback. It needs no new host setting because current verified source-form provider already owns a stable private key/revision. Neither variant is implemented or qualified yet.

A private snapshot alternative creates bounded durable per-review frozen table and context under a random opaque ID, expiring after15minutes; commits restore that exact table and require current identical app/actor/team/session plus per-row authority.
